text:
Cam - People Ops: Quick company-wide update: were rolling out a Travel Safety & Code of Conduct refresh today. Main changes: 1) domestic business trips under 72 hours are now auto-approved if youve completed Travel Safety microtraining; 2) all international travel requires pre-approval + security screening; 3) expanded conduct reporting options while traveling. Full policy: https://redwoodintra.company/policies/travel-conduct-refresh

Ivy - Travel Safety: TL;DR: Auto-approval = no manual manager sign-off for trips <72h (business), but you must submit the Travel Form and have the training completed in the last 24 months. Auto-approval still requires a calendar invite and risk checkbox filled.

Ben: Where's the Travel Form? Any required fields we should watch out for?

Ivy - Travel Safety: Form link in the policy doc. Required fields: destination, dates, emergency contact, hotel name, itinerary, and risk checkbox. Minimal snippet: `destination, start_date, end_date, emergency_contact, itinerary, risk_ack`. If you travel to high-risk countries, the form routes to Security.

Mika - Legal: Note on conduct: harassment or discrimination incidents while on travel can be reported via the normal channels or anonymously through EthicsLine. We added a travel-specific incident flow so manager notifications are delayed until the employee requests it. Protecting the traveler's choice is priority.

Ben: What's considered "high-risk"? And how strict is the screening?

Ivy - Travel Safety: High-risk = countries flagged by our Travel Advisory (link in doc) or regions with active advisories from public sources. Screening is a short security check + confirmation of emergency evac options; typically 24-48hr turnaround. For urgent travel, contact travel-safety@redwood.com and include "expedite" in the subject.

Cam - People Ops: A few operational notes: 1) Home Office Stipend still applies for remote work but not for business travel; 2) travel expenses must follow the expense policy; 3) managers: you can still override auto-approval in edge cases (flag the request and ping people-ops).

Ben: Any tax impact for hotel upgrades / per diems?

Mika - Legal: Usual rules apply: personal upgrades are taxable if expensed. Per diems are non-taxable within policy limits; see Payroll FAQ. Payroll-Bot will post a summary in the doc.

HR-Bot: Policy PDF uploaded: https://redwoodintra.company/policies/travel-conduct-refresh.pdf. Travel Safety microtraining assigned to all employees; completion deadline: 45 days. Manager dashboard shows completions.

Cam - People Ops: We're hosting two town halls: Manager ops + Q&A Thursday 9:30am PT; All-hands info drop Friday 11:00am PT. RSVP links in the policy doc. If you have specific cross-border cases, DM Ivy or open a ticket with travel-safety.
